supersessionRule: one current verdict per family, ordered by the base each row DECLARES it read at: a read whose verifiedAtBase descends from another read's base is the later one and supersedes it. Where neither base is an ancestor of the other, a row that declares a commit-shaped base outranks one that declares none. Lane precedence (factory vf lanes over codex-cloud directories, then higher lane number) decides only when neither row says when it read. failedObligations.finding: The packet asserts a silence the repository does not have. Its "The filing fee" section reads the petition's paragraph 3 correctly — a sworn statement that fees "mandated by A.C.A § 16-90-1419" have been paid — and correctly reports that no amount is printed on the form, which this lane confirmed by extracting the source PDF's text (paragraph 3 names the fee statute and no figure appears anywhere on the face). But it then tells the participant that "no source this packet holds establishes it" and sends them to ask the clerk what the § 16-90-1419 fee is. The repository establishes it. The compiled Arkansas profile — cited as a requiredSourceId for this exact route in the national route census — states it three separate ways: packetGenerator.feeRules[1] "Sealing petition filing fee $0 — Filing fees eliminated by the 2019 amendments", feeRules[0] "Act 1460 eliminated sealing filing fees; the real costs are records and any counsel", and filingDestinationRules[1] "File in the circuit or district court that handled the case. Act 1460 eliminated filing fees for sealing." The profile's sourceFormStatements[7] ties this to the very form in this packet: "Petition and Order to Seal Arrest (Act 1460) — Arrest records under § 16-90-1409." Amendment A1 settles the ordering: ask first whether the repository establishes the answer; if it does, the packet states it, and a named checkable authority may stand in only where no held source establishes it. Here one does, so the stand-in is unavailable and the packet substitutes a question for an answer the repository holds. The consequence is not cosmetic: paragraph 3 is sworn, and a participant told to go and pay an unknown fee before signing is being sent to resolve something the repository says was abolished in 2019. The repair is for a repairer with the legal record in front of them, not for this lane: state what the profile holds and reconcile it with the form's paragraph 3, which still recites the fee statute. Whether the correct sentence is "$0, fees eliminated by the 2019 amendments" or a reconciliation of the two is a drafting and counsel question; asserting repository silence is not an available answer.

failedObligations.finding: The service mechanics are right and the objection clock is wrong in a way that can mislead a felony-class petitioner. Correct: two recipients from the form's own Certificate of Service (the prosecuting or city attorney, and the arresting agency), the form's two methods, and the rule that the certificate is completed only after service. The defect is the objection window. The packet leads with a flat "The prosecuting attorney has 30 days to object", sourced to the committed packet-set manifest. I traced that sentence: it is data/record-clearing/legal-design-intake/AR.memo.json rules.service, and it appears VERBATIM on 11 of the 12 Arkansas tracks in that file — including ar-felony-seal, where the same repository's compiled profile says the window is 90 days. A line that is provably wrong on a sibling track it is attached to is state-level boilerplate, not a route-addressed determination, and under A3 (holding is per FACT, not per document) it does not establish this route's answer. The record that DOES address it is the compiled profile's own table: "Prosecutor objection window - misdemeanor 30 days / felony 90 days, Receipt / filing of petition". That rule is self-applying here, because the delivered petition prints "A Class _____ [_] felony [_] misdemeanor" and the participant supplies the class. So the repository establishes a determinate class-keyed rule and the packet publishes a flat number from a non-route-held line, demoting the real rule to "the longer window MAY apply to you". It then sends a statutory question to an office that cannot answer it: "ask the clerk of the court where you file which window that court runs" — the window is set by statute, not by court practice, and A1 permits a named authority to stand in only where no held source establishes the fact. The contrast is inside this same builder's own work: ar-misdemeanor-dwi-seal-set resolves the identical conflict correctly by naming its route's class ("this packet is a misdemeanour DWI or BWI conviction, which puts it in the 30-day limb"). The repair is one paragraph: state the class rule as the rule, cite the profile, and drop the clerk sentence. Recorded separately: the three-day service deadline comes only from that same 11-track boilerplate — the compiled profile contains no "three days" and the form prints none — but it errs toward serving early, so I record it as a provenance limit rather than a failure.

failedObligations.finding: The canonical completeness gate refuses this family outright. Run here, verify-packet-completeness.mjs returns FAIL_COMPONENT_SET at 0/0 written with auditable:false and the finding 'the field map uses a schema this verifier does not read; it is refused rather than read as empty'. The cause is exact and reproducible: readFieldRows() accepts four shapes — top-level writes/refusals, top-level maps, documents[].fields[].decision, and documents[].writableAnchors + documents[].withheld — and this family's production-field-map.json uses none of them. Its documents carry writeBoxes, withheldBeforeTheFactory, roleRefusals, refusedByTheFactory and protectedRulesHandedToTheFactory instead, so `shape` stays null and the verifier early-returns before counting anything. By direct read the three component roles the packet-set manifest declares are all present — process_guidance as participant-instructions.md, primary_filing as the ACIC petition, proposed_order as the ACIC order — so no component is missing and the repair is the field-map schema, not the packet. Recorded as FAIL and not as an environment limitation because the contract's own words are that an unreadable field map is refused rather than read as empty, and because a family the completeness gate cannot audit cannot be shown complete.

THE PACKET GIVES A VENUE ANSWER THE REPOSITORY RECORDS AS NOT EXISTING FOR HALF THE DISPOSITIONS IT SHIPS, AND TELLS THE PARTICIPANT THEY NEED NOT WORK VENUE OUT. participant-instructions.md, under 'Where this goes', says: 'File the petition and the unsigned order together in the court where the nolle prosequi or dismissal order was entered. That is the committed packet-set manifest's own instruction for this packet, and it is the answer: you do not have to work out venue for yourself.' THE PACKET SHIPS FOUR DISPOSITIONS: its own paragraph 2 offers nolle prosequi, dismissal, judgment of acquittal, and charges never filed, and the instructions tell the participant to tick exactly one of the four. THE REPOSITORY ANSWERS VENUE FOR ONLY TWO OF THEM, and says so three times. (1) The committed route census row for obligation:track-only:AR:ar-nonconviction-seal records destination.detail '§ 16-90-1410(b). Venue for an acquittal and for charges never filed is not stated.' failedObligations.finding: The repair added a well-drafted section that names a checkable authority, and it still fails, because it asserts a silence the repository does not have. The section states: "No held source establishes what it costs to file a CPL 160.59 sealing application", that neither application source states a filing fee, states that filing is free, or describes a fee waiver, and that the packet "does not supply a figure it does not hold" — then names the clerk's office of the court of conviction and sentencing as the office to ask. The claim about the two forms is correct and this lane confirmed it independently: extracting the text of both the application and the pro se packet from the mounted corpus finds no fee, cost or dollar figure anywhere on either face. But the claim about the repository is false. The compiled New York profile, cited as a requiredSourceId for this exact route, answers it directly: packetGenerator.feeRules[2] reads "CPL 160.59 sealing application — No separate filing fee — Court motion; notarization needed", and the profile's narrative repeats it — "the 160.59 motion itself carries no separate filing fee" — and its agent guidance says to note that the motion has no separate filing fee. Amendment A1 settles the ordering: ask first whether the repository establishes the answer, and a named checkable authority may stand in only where none does. One does here, so the stand-in is unavailable and the packet sends the participant to ask a question the repository already answers. The packet's third paragraph shows it can do this correctly — it states the certificate-of-disposition fee, $5 outside New York City and $10 in the five boroughs, sourced to the form's own face, and the compiled profile's feeRules[0] and [1] hold exactly those figures. The repair is to state the no-separate-filing-fee answer the profile holds alongside the certificate fee it already states, and to carry across the waiver-adjacent facts the profile also holds — that legal-aid organisations and county district attorney sealing units assist pro se applicants at no cost.

failedObligations.finding: ON EVERY ONE OF THE THREE PETITIONS, THE PACKET ASKS THE PARTICIPANT TO HAND-WRITE FACTS IT HAS ALREADY PRINTED ON THE SAME PAGE. Measured on the delivered canonical bytes. Each petition carries a section B 'THE PETITIONER' stating 'Date of birth: 1991-04-17', a caption reading 'IN RE: Jordan Avery Reyes, PETITIONER.', and a footer block 'PRINTED NAME: Jordan Avery Reyes / MAILING ADDRESS: 42 Magnolia Street, Springfield 62704 / TELEPHONE: 555-0142 / EMAIL: jordan.reyes@example.org'. Between them, section C asks as empty dotted blanks: '[C1 - full name] What is your full legal name, and any other name the case is under?', '[C2 - date of birth] What is your date of birth?', and '[C3 - mailing address] What is your current address, phone number and email?'. The same three appear at lines 52/56/60, 347/351/355 and 660/664/668 of the extracted canonical text -- once per petition, nine duplicated asks in one delivered packet -- and the instructions' items table repeats all three per route. C1 has a legitimate extra limb (any other name the case is under) and C4, county of residence, is genuinely not held; C2 and C3 have no such excuse. This is the A4 class: a packet may never tell a participant it does not state something it does state, and printing 'What is your date of birth?' as a blank one inch below 'Date of birth: 1991-04-17' does exactly that. The harm is concrete on a pleading -- a participant who complies writes their name and date of birth twice on one petition, and a clerk reading two entries has an inconsistency to resolve; a participant who does not comply is left unsure whether they have skipped a required item. The packet's own framing shows the intent it missed: it says every item in section C is a fact 'about your own case' that 'belongs to the record itself', which is true of C5-C17 and false of C1-C3. The repair is to drop C2 and C3 and narrow C1 to the alias limb.

On four of the five routes the rendered component set matches its committed packet-set manifest exactly. On the fifth it does not, and the counter cannot see it. The manifest for nd-marijuana-first-offense-seal-set declares three components: nd-marijuana-first-offense-seal-primary-filing-1 [required], nd-marijuana-first-offense-seal-proposed-order-2 [conditional] and nd-marijuana-first-offense-seal-legal-effect-explanation-3 [required], role legal_effect_explanation, titled 'What sealing does, and what it does not do'. The delivered packet renders primary-filing-1, proposed-order-2 and nd-marijuana-first-offense-seal-filing-instructions-3 — a different componentId with a different role. The manifest-required legal_effect_explanation component is not in the packet under any id. FOUR committed records agree on the id the packet omits: legal-design-packet-set-manifests.json, legal-design-track-registry.json, packet-specifications/ND-first-offense-possession-sealing.v1.json (as manifestComponentId) and the route obligation census (participantFacingInstrument). This family's OWN production-field-map.json contradicts its own delivered set: at line 110 it records the instrument for this route as '...legal_effect_explanation: nd-marijuana-first-offense-seal-legal-effect-explanation-3'. requiredComponentsMissing measured 0 in a fresh completeness run in this lane, because that counter compares the rendered set against the family's own componentSet rather than against the committed manifest. The substitution is not merely a naming mismatch. The committed packet specification gives the missing component three named static sections and only one survives anywhere in the delivered bytes. 'What the order does' (the seal is irreversible; the record may not be opened even by court order) IS carried, on the filing-instructions page and in participant-instructions.md. 'What it does not reach' is NOT carried in any form: its required text is 'The order is directed at the court record. It does not by itself change records held by other agencies, and it is not a pardon. If you need a criminal-history record corrected as well, that is a separate request to the agency that holds it.' Grepping this route's six delivered pages (canonical 29-34) for its distinguishing terms returns nothing — 'other agencies' 0, 'not a pardon' 0, 'is not a pardon' 0, 'criminal history' 0, 'criminal-history record' 0, 'separate request' 0; the single hit for 'does not reach' on those pages is 'Other charges in the same case, which the subsection does not reach', a different proposition. participant-instructions.md carries none of it either. 'This is not the general sealing chapter' survives only as the half-sentence 'which makes this seal stronger than Chapter 12-60.1 sealing'; its required content — that 12-60.1's three-and-five-year waiting periods, its clear-and-convincing burden and its no-hearing-before-45-days rule do not apply here — is absent from this route's pages. That omission is participant-facing and it is made worse by the packet's own contents: the SAME artifact tells the participant three separate times, on the three Chapter 12-60.1 routes, that 'Sealing under Chapter 12-60.1 does not reach BCI criminal history record information or the criminal justice data system, and it does not reach federal, tribal, military, out-of-state or private-database records', and prints 'clear-and-convincing' and '45 days' on those pages. A participant on the marijuana route reads that this seal is 'stronger than Chapter 12-60.1 sealing' and is never told that it too is directed only at the court record. The plainest reading available to them is the wrong one.

failedObligations.finding: Three sentences print a POINTER in the grammatical position of the FACT, and the packet's own design turns that into a participant-facing defect. In all four tracks, paragraph 5 reads "Applicant was charged with Possession offense shown on the certified disposition by [ARRESTING AGENCY MUST BE CONFIRMED]", paragraph 7 reads "The matter was resolved with the following disposition: Disposition shown on the certified disposition", and paragraph 8 reads "Applicant may be eligible for sealing on the following basis: Eligibility is not certified by this artifact; source review and local-court confirmation are required." The first two state where to find a fact in the slot where the fact belongs; the third puts the factory's own non-certification language into a pleading's eligibility allegation. This matters because of what the instructions ask the participant to do with the document: "Transfer only reviewed content to that form." The bracketed ALL-CAPS markers are self-evidently not transferable and the top-level instructions name every one of them and say what to supply instead. These three sentences carry no such marking, sit in ordinary prose, and are not transferable content — paragraph 8 is affirmatively wrong to copy onto a court form. The fix is to mark them as unresolved in the same way the bracketed items are, or to omit the clause rather than print a pointer as an allegation.

failedObligations.finding: The packet denies a rule the repository states, and the denial costs the participant a real limb. It says: "No held source in this packet names a statewide Ohio filing office or a statewide application." Under A2 the repository includes the compiled state profile, and src/lib/rcap-engine/compiled/profiles/OH-ohio.json states the rule plainly and repeatedly, keyed to these sections: "File in the sentencing court for an Ohio conviction or in a court of common pleas for an out-of-state or federal conviction", and for § 2953.35 "The application is filed in the sentencing court". A1 as amended settles the order of operations — ask first whether the repository establishes the answer; if it does, the packet states it. The consequence is not cosmetic: the packet's substitute answer, "the Ohio court that handled the case", silently drops the out-of-state and federal conviction limb, and a participant in that position is sent to a court that is not in Ohio at all. The repair is to state the profile's two-limb rule.

failedObligations.finding: The packet tells the participant that it does not state an amount that its own delivered pages print. participant-instructions.md carries, in bold: "The BCI certificate carries a separate fee, and this packet does not state an amount because BCI sets it per applicant." The canonical fixture this family ships prints "$65.00" three times on packet pages 17 and 18, on the BCI Application for Certificate of Eligibility the packet itself delivers. Confirmed in this lane with pdftotext against this family's own committed bytes (SHA-256 8efb78f3f885af303bc74f461172d319f63b60bb747720329e401c1bd4d417f4), not taken from any brief or report. DET-FEE-AND-WAIVER-001 amendment A4 states the rule in one line: a packet may never tell a participant that it does not state something it does state. A SECOND and independent limb fails here, and it is the A1/A2/A3 one rather than A4's internal-consistency rule. The compiled Utah state profile (src/lib/rcap-engine/compiled/profiles/UT-utah.json, SHA-256 73dd7ea988d0673dca3b8bf657f2df090d062c0821f8c0662a57ccfac8e7660d) states: "eligible conviction, plea-in-abeyance, or special certificates may require an additional $65 per case; no certificate issuance fee is required for dismissals, acquittals, or declinations." This route is a dismissal without prejudice. Applying A3's per-fact, per-route test rather than reading the document as a whole: the exempting limb names "dismissals" without qualification, and the limb that does carry a charge names conviction, plea-in-abeyance and special certificates, none of which is this route. A dismissal without prejudice is a dismissal and is not a plea in abeyance, so the exemption reaches it. The repository therefore establishes that the certificate issuance fee for this route is nil, and A2 lists the compiled state profile for the family's jurisdiction as a held source in its own right. The packet nonetheless tells the participant that it cannot state the amount and sends them to ask BCI — which is precisely what A1 forbids where the record already answers. The residual ambiguity is stated rather than resolved: the profile's word is "dismissals", unqualified, and a lane wanting certainty should read the BCI FAQ the profile cites before publishing $0. What passes on this obligation is not in dispute and is recorded so the repair does not disturb it: the court filing fee of $150 is stated and sourced to the row the packet fills on 1044XX page 2, and the court waiver route is named as Utah form 1305GE under Utah Code 78A-2-302 and CJA Rule 4-508.

Ask the Bureau of Criminal Identification what your certificates cost and whether you qualify for its fee waiver; do not assume the court's $150 waiver covers BCI's fee, because they are two different offices.

failedObligations.evidence: All 38 reported writes per fixture are readable from normalized PDF text, but the route is expressly for an arrest where charges were never filed and therefore has no pre-existing court case. Nevertheless the build writes matter.case_number into 1000EX and three locations in 1020EX (canonical 24-CR-001234; boundary 2026-CR-900123-EXTENDED-CASE-IDENTIFIER). The controlling track says no case exists, and the current Utah Courts instruction says that if there is no case number the court will give one. Treating a fictional pre-existing criminal case number as a known prefill is route-incompatible.

The packet identifies the certificate, 180-day certificate life, payment, identification, fingerprints, signatures, venue details, public-interest statement, complete case history and final-declination evidence. It omits two route-specific prerequisites: the at-least-30-days-since-arrest threshold held in the track registry and current Utah Courts instructions, and the instruction that this never-charged route has no existing case number and the court assigns one. Instead the fixtures prefill a criminal case number. A participant can follow every listed before-filing instruction and still file too early or carry a phantom case number.

Stage one correctly names Utah BCI, but stage two says to file in the district court 'for the county where the case was heard' and to use the court listed for that case. This route has no filed case. The controlling track and current Utah Courts instructions instead require the district court in the county/district where the arrest occurred. The later statement that the county is written 'from your case' repeats the wrong premise.

The packet affirmatively directs the participant to mail or email the prosecutor copies and then fill service method/address/date. The controlling track registry and current Utah Courts process say the opposite: when the participant files, the court sends the filing to the prosecuting attorney and the petitioner does not effect ordinary service. The participant-facing instruction imports the BCI handout's conflicting older step and can cause unauthorized or duplicative service.
